title: The Church a Garden Is
description: The Church a Garden Is in Tonic Solfa to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 103, “The Barren fig-tree. Lk 13:6-9”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR); any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The church a gar-den is In which be-liev-ers stand, Like or-na-men-tal trees Plant-ed by God's own hand: His Spir-it wa-ters all their roots, And ev-ery branch a-bounds with fruits.

lines: His Spirit waters all their roots,
And every branch abounds with fruits.
No fruits of grace are on them found,
They stand but cumb'rers of the ground.
In vain his strength he spends,
He hears the Lord his will make known,
To cut the barren fig-trees down.
His last relief is earnest prayer,
Lord, spare them yet another year.
Spare them, and let me try
Who knows but yet they fruit may yield!
If not--'tis just, they must be felled.
At length he'll strike the threatened blow,
And lay the barren fig-tree low.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
